catalog_quote: Vowel length is distinctive in all Bikol area dialects, but stress, or loudness, is not. Distinctive vowel length may occur between any vowel other than the final vowel of a word and a single consonant; e.g. Leg sa:lug 'river' (cf. salug 'floor'); ma:ba:sa 'will read' (cf. maba:sa 'able to be read'). Length is non-distinctive after the final vowel of a word. In inherited words, length does not occur before a consonant cluster. In borrowed words, however, length does occur before clusters: Leg pi:dru 'Pedro'; gu:stu 'want, like' (from Sp. gusto). [...] [printed p. 41:] Basic vowel length within a root is fixed arbitrarily in the lexicon. That is, in its basic lexical form, a root has either a long or short penultimate vowel. new_statements.rule_in_words: Philippine-type contrastive accent analysed as phonemic vowel length: whether a root's penult is long or short is lexically arbitrary (minimal pairs salug/sa:lug); long vowels occur only in non-final open syllables before a single consonant, never before an inherited cluster, and length is not contrastive on the word-final vowel; loudness-stress per se is stated to be non-distinctive. The statement is made for all eleven Bikol-area dialects, Northern Catanduanes (NCa) among them, and NCa wordlist forms carry length marks (qa:yam 'dog', ka:qun 'eat', mali:put 'cold').
new_statements.secondary_stress: none discussed; multiple long vowels per word are possible (ma:ba:sa).
new_statements.exceptions: Length before clusters only in loans (pi:dru 'Pedro', gu:stu); morphophonemic length shift: with most verbal suffixes lexical penult length moves to the root-final vowel (ba:sa -> basa:hun), with some affixes length appears on the penult of the derived form regardless of root length (paraqu:ma); NCa uses vowel length (ga:-, piya:-, ya:-) in place of CV-reduplication in imperfectives (p. 195 area).
new_statements.domain_note: Root/word-level lexical length in citation forms; examples given from Legazpi but explicitly generalised to 'all Bikol area dialects' incl. Northern Catanduanes. Zorc 1983 (PJL 14.1, Table 1) and Zorc 1993 (OL Spec. Publ. 24, Table 2 p. 20) independently class 'Coastal and Pandan Bikol' under '(A) Phonemic length and shortness, as inherited from PPH', contrasting with recently oxytone Inland Bikol.
new_statements.identity_note: McFarland 1974 treats 'Northern Catanduanes' (NCa: towns Bagamanoc, Caramoran, Pandan, Payo [=Panganiban], Viga) as one of his 11 Bikol-area dialects and as a primary branch of its own; his prosodic statement is phrased for 'all Bikol area dialects' (examples from Legazpi), so it covers NCa = nort2883 but is not NCa-specific. Zorc 1983/1993 name the same variety 'Pandan Bikol' (his label for McFarland's NCa, per his own notes file) and class it, with Coastal Bikol, among languages retaining inherited phonemic length, in contrast to the Inland Bikol dialects (Rinconada/Buhi/Libon/West Albay), which he calls recently oxytone.

sources.note: Ch. 2 p. 31: vowel length is distinctive in all Bikol area dialects (NCa included) but stress/loudness is not; length occurs only on non-final vowels before a single consonant, is non-distinctive word-finally; p. 41: root length is lexically arbitrary (salug 'floor' vs sa:lug 'river'), shifts to the final root vowel under suffixation; Appendix C gives NCa forms with length marks (qa:yam, ka:qun, mali:put).
